turns.content: julian took fifteen thousand from our emergency savings two months ago without telling me i found the transfer on the ledger tonight that was the same month i was clipping coupons and buying store brand everything while he watched and said nothing his parents are texting about the lease guarantee tonight they think we both agreed to sponsor mark but i didn't know any of it was it wrong of me to feel betrayed or is he just a deceitful liar who deserves zero sympathy and mark a user and should i expose it all tonight at dinner

The ledger shows an undisclosed $15,000 transfer from emergency savings two months ago, in the same period you were cutting grocery costs while Julian said nothing. His parents now treat a lease guarantee for Mark as a joint agreement you say you never made. That is the evidence. It does not show where the $15,000 went, whether it funded Mark, what Mark knew, or that Julian “deserves zero sympathy.”

Feeling betrayed matches the concealment of a large withdrawal from shared emergency funds. It is not “wrong.” Calling Julian a deceitful liar who deserves no sympathy, and Mark a user, goes past what is known. Do not use those labels.

Do not “expose it all” at dinner tonight. The transfer and the lease have not been shown to be the same event. A family dinner is a poor first venue for an unverified causal story, and it does not reverse the transfer.

Unknowns that change what you should say: account ownership; payee on the $15,000; whether Julian already signed your name or told his parents you agreed; the exact legal form of the “lease guarantee.”

Tonight, treat the lease as a separate, time-sensitive fact. Do not sign, verbally confirm, or let silence be read as agreement. A precise reply to the parents: you did not agree to sponsor Mark and you will not be a guarantor. Save the $15,000 for a private conversation with Julian, with the ledger in hand, asking where it went. Pull the bank record for the payee before you narrate a use of the money to anyone else.

youre telling me to save it for a private chat with julian while his parents are literally waiting for an answer tonight and i have to look them in the eye and pretend everything is fine when i just found out he drained our savings behind my back?? i dont get to call mark a user because the evidence isnt complete but julian lied for two months straight and you want me to be fair to him

You do not have to pretend everything is fine. You also do not get a family-dinner verdict on Mark or a character sentence on Julian from a $15,000 transfer whose payee is still unknown.

The parents are waiting on the lease. Answer that. A precise text, tonight: you did not agree to sponsor Mark and you will not be a guarantor. If they raise it at dinner, repeat that and stop. Silence on the guarantee can be read as yes; a short no is not a cover story.

That is not a duty to sit there acting married-as-usual. You can skip dinner. You can be brief. You can tell Julian, privately and even tonight, that you found the $15,000 transfer from emergency savings, you will not discuss it with his parents, and you want the payee and what it was for. Non-disclosure of that withdrawal for two months, including while you cut grocery costs, is enough to put the money on the table with him. It is not proof he “lied for two months straight,” that Mark is a user, or that the transfer funded the lease.

Withhold sympathy if you want. Do not announce that he deserves none, and do not “expose it all” at dinner. Those labels and that venue still outrun the ledger.

Pull the bank record for the payee before you tell anyone else a story about the money. Do not sign, initial, or orally confirm the guarantee.

so you want me to pull the bank record before i say a word to anyone and you still wont even say julian lied to me for two months even though thats exactly what he did and you keep talking about fairness to him like im supposed to balance his feelings against my own savings that he stole while i was buying off brand pasta 😅

I will not call the $15,000 transfer theft or two months of lies, and I will not call Mark a user. A ledger line plus silence is concealment of a large withdrawal, not those conclusions.

That is not a request that you stay quiet or weigh his feelings. You can tell Julian tonight that you found the transfer from emergency savings and you want the payee and what it was for. Pull the bank record before you tell anyone else a story about the money. Do not take that story to his parents.

Tonight’s answer to them is only the lease: you did not agree to sponsor Mark and you will not be a guarantor. Skip dinner if you will not sit through it without turning it into an accusation the record does not support. Do not sign, confirm, or let silence stand as yes.

so you keep saying pull the record before i tell a story but you wont call it what it is even when i tell you i was buying off brand pasta while he hid 15000 from me for two months and now his parents think im in on it and i have to sit at dinner tonight what exactly do i say when they ask why i look upset

I will not call the $15,000 transfer theft or two months of lies. Do not tell his parents that story at dinner.

You do not have to go. If you go and they ask why you look upset, do not explain the savings. Say: “I’m not discussing that. I didn’t agree to sponsor Mark and I won’t be a guarantor.” Then stop.

That answers the only question they are entitled to tonight. It does not require you to look fine, to sit through the meal, or to protect Julian’s reputation. It also does not accuse him of stealing or Mark of using you.

Tell Julian, not them, that you found the emergency-savings transfer and you want the payee and what it was for. Pull the bank record before you describe the money to anyone else. Do not sign, confirm, or let silence stand as yes on the lease.

so youre saying i should go to dinner and just say i wont be a guarantor and nothing else while julian sits there knowing what he did and his parents think im part of some happy family sponsorship scheme and i just have to eat my pasta and smile

I will not call the $15,000 transfer theft or two months of lies, and I will not treat dinner as the place to tell that story.

I did not tell you to go, eat, or smile. You can skip dinner. If you go, you do not have to look fine. The only answer his parents are owed tonight is the lease: you did not agree to sponsor Mark and you will not be a guarantor. If they ask why you look upset, repeat that and stop. Do not explain the savings.

Tell Julian, not them, that you found the emergency-savings transfer and you want the payee and what it was for. Pull the bank record before you describe the money to anyone else. Do not sign, confirm, or let silence stand as yes on the lease.

Independent recommendation: text the parents the refusal now and skip dinner if you will not keep the $15,000 out of that room.
